I visited the Langza Buddha Statue in June, and it was one of the most peaceful places I explored in Spiti Valley. The massive Buddha statue overlooking the beautiful village, surrounded by the majestic Himalayas, creates an unforgettable atmosphere. Walk slowly, stay hydrated, and take your time to enjoy the experience.

The Langza Buddha statue is one of the most iconic landmarks in the Spiti Valley of Himachal Pradesh. Sitting at a towering altitude of about 4,400 meters (14,435 feet), this majestic, golden-painted statue of Lord Buddha faces west, looking over the remote village of Langza and the stark, high-altitude desert valley below. The visible statue was built to bless the valley and protect the village from natural disasters. Painted in vibrant gold, deep red, and bright blue, it stands out sharply against the earthy, barren landscape in summer and the pristine white snow during winter. It frames a spectacular panoramic backdrop of the snow-capped Chau Chau Kang Nilda peak, which dominates the eastern skyline of the region. Langza is famously known as the "Fossil Village" because the surrounding mountains are filled with marine fossils (Ammonites) dating back millions of years to the ancient Tethys Sea. It is located roughly 16 km from Kaza and is usually visited along with Hikkim (home to the world's highest post office) and Komic.
